description: NATS and MQTT spans OBI exported in KinD (Kubernetes 1.34) from nats-server 2.11.17 with JetStream (in the cluster, on the host network, and outside the cluster where OBI cannot name it), nats.js 2.29.3 clients (core pub/sub, request-reply, a JetStream producer, an acking pull and push consumer, an app whose service.name is "nats") and mosquitto 2 with MQTT clients, under the kubernetes-agent chart's rendered OBI DaemonSet and config. Clients connected before OBI started, then again under it.

body: what OBI exported, as a collector's file exporter wrote it (OTLP/JSON), at most two spans per shape, OBI version and service.peer.name presence; resource attributes trimmed to the ones ingest reads.

spans: per span, OBI's own event type as its trace printer (OTEL_EBPF_TRACE_PRINTER=text) logged it, the workload's role, and the kind to store: SERVER for every *Server event type but a client's split delivery naming its broker (C2, kept as exported), SERVER for a MSG a broker wrote (B4), and the exported kind for every other client-typed span. v013Kind is the kind OBI v0.13 gives the same span.

captures.v0.13.0-genericgo: OBI v0.13.0 with the chart's config and the generic tracer
captures.v0.13.0-gotracer: OBI v0.13.0 with the chart's config and the Go tracer, which records no NATS span of nats-server

shapes.C1: NATS client: its PUB (client-typed), server.address names the broker's Service, equal ports
shapes.C1 host-network broker: C1 against a host-network nats-server, through its Service
shapes.C1 external broker: C1 against a broker outside the cluster: server.address is its IP
shapes.C1 app named like broker: C1 of an application whose service.name is the broker's ("nats")
shapes.C2: NATS client: the MSG OBI split off its ack, pull or request (NATSServer, unreversed): server.address the broker, server.port its listening port, network.peer the client itself
shapes.C2 host-network broker: C2 from a host-network nats-server, through its Service
shapes.C2 external broker: C2 from a broker OBI cannot name: server.address falls back to the client's own service name
shapes.C2 app named like broker: C2 of an application whose service.name is the broker's: server.address equals its own name
shapes.C3: NATS client: a MSG OBI reversed (NATSServer): server.address the client's own name, server.port its ephemeral port
shapes.B2: nats-server: a MSG it delivered, consistently oriented (NATSServer)
shapes.B3: nats-server: the MSG OBI split off a MSG + PUB exchange the broker wrote first (NATSServer, unreversed): server.address the subscriber, server.port its ephemeral port, network.peer the broker itself
shapes.B3-main: nats-server: the PUB of that exchange, typed client-side (NATSClient): equal ports, the subscriber named
shapes.B4: nats-server: a MSG it wrote, typed client-side (NATSClient): equal ports, the subscriber named
shapes.host-network B1: B1 on a host-network nats-server: server.address names the node
shapes.host-network B2: B2 on a host-network nats-server: server.address names the node
shapes.MQTT client reversed delivery: MQTT subscriber: a PUBLISH delivered to it, reversed (MQTTServer)
shapes.MQTT broker receiving-side: mosquitto: a PUBLISH or SUBSCRIBE it read (MQTTServer)
shapes.MQTT broker publish: mosquitto: a PUBLISH it delivered to a subscriber, typed client-side (MQTTClient): kept PRODUCER, as v0.13 sent it
